title: Fans share memories of rugby league legend Sir Billy Boston

evidence_packet.title: Fans share memories of rugby league legend Sir Billy Boston
evidence_packet.lead: Hundreds of fans went to Robin Park Arena to sign a book of condolence for the Wigan Warriors star
evidence_packet.summary: Hundreds of fans went to Robin Park Arena to sign a book of condolence for the Wigan Warriors star
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fans share memories of rugby league legend Sir Billy Boston - BBC News Image caption, Hundreds of fans have paid tribute to Sir Billy Boston by signing the book of condolence at Robin Park Arena By Yunus Mulla Reporting from Wigan Published 1 hour ago Fans have shared memories of the much-loved rugby league legend Sir Billy Boston and signed a book of condolence at his former club Wigan Warriors. Rugby league's first knight died earlier this week aged 92 surrounded by his closest family, the club said. As well as his achievements on the pitch - including scoring 571 tries in his career - a total surpassed only by Australian legend Brian Bevan in top-class rugby league - Boston has a legion of fans heartbroken at the legend's death. The club's kitman, and a lifelong fan who first saw him as a child, and decades later worked for him in his pub when he retired, were among hundreds who went to Robin Park Arena to pay tribute to the star. Image source, PA Media Image caption, Billy Boston who was rugby league's first knight died on Tuesday aged 92 Josie Andrews held back the tears as she told BBC North West Tonight : "I fell in love with Billy Boston when I was eight. "My dad took me to watch him and that is when I fell in love with Wigan rugby." She said she later worked for Boston when he ran the Griffin Hotel close to Wigan's Central Park Ground after he retired from the game. Image caption, Josie Andrews fought back tears as she described how she fell in love with him when her dad took her to watch him at eight Another fan paying his respects was David Mullen who said he met the great man twice and described him as an "absolute gent". "At the ground we always saw Sir Billy and what an absolute guy he was." Image caption, David Mullen Standard bearer for Royal British Leg

evidence_packet.summary: The Bolton comedian is putting on a show in Blackpool to help Fin Cormack get heart treatment in the US
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Peter Kay is to perform a one-off show in Blackpool next month to raise funds for a teenager's vital heart operation Fin Cormack, from Prenton, Merseyside, has a rare condition called Ebstein's anomaly and has had several major heart surgeries, with his first when he was just 11 days old Now 19, his family are trying to pay for treatment for him in the United States and the Bolton comedian said he was inspired to do the special show at the Opera House in Blackpool's Winter Gardens on 27 September after seeing his story on the news Fin's mum said the family were "bowled over" by the star's incredible gesture Ebstein's anomaly is an abnormality of the tricuspid valve that you were born with, according to the NHS The family said they were trying to raise £200,000 for treatment from a leading expert on the condition, Dr Dearani, at the Mayo Clinic in the USA, "to give Fin something he's never really had: the chance at a fuller, easier life"

Red Bank was one of Manchester's industrial heartlands and was once home to dye works and mills which made use of the River Irk as a water supply It later became part the city's rail infrastructure and the site of the railway sidings and sheds

In an email sent to George House Trust users and seen by the BBC, the Manchester-based organisation said the material had been downloaded by hackers but not published. The breach is part of a wider cyber security incident potentially affecting up to 1,500 charities across the UK. George House Trust said it was investigating and "taking all appropriate steps". The charity, which was set up in 1985, provides support, advice and information to thousands of people living with HIV. It is unclear how many people connected to the trust have been affected by the breach. The email said personal information including addresses, emails, telephone numbers and "notes and records" about users engagement with the charity was on the database that was targeted. However, it said there was "no sign that any of the data or information" had been "misused in any way at this time". Review carried out The security incident involves technology company Beacon, which operates a database system used by more than a thousand charities across the country. Beacon said the data breach happened at the end of July and it "immediately engaged external cyber security experts to help contain the incident and investigate". The company said it was supporting all the organisations affected. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Dove Stone residents fear parking 'nightmare' after beauty spot reopens - BBC News Image source, Local Democracy Reporting Service Image caption, The beauty spot has been plagued by parking problems, such as here in April 2026 By Ed Barnes , Local Democracy Reporting Service and Haider Saleem , North West , Reporting from North West Published 26 August 2026 People living near a Greater Manchester beauty spot fear a return to a "nightmare" of car-jammed roads and litter after the area reopened following a wildfire. Dove Stone reservoir, near Greenfield in Oldham reopened last week after the blaze burned for more than three weeks. Residents said the area had previously been plagued by obstructed roads, while visitors also left litter and lit barbecues, raising concerns about access for emergency vehicles - and now they fear a return of the same issues. Oldham Council said wardens patrolled the area and issued 946 penalty charge notices around the reservoir in 2025. The RSPB, which manages the attraction's car park, said it understood the concerns. The wildfire began on 11 July and was declared a major incident, with people told to avoid the area while firefighters tackled the blaze. The incident was stood down on 3 August, although crews remained at the scene for days afterwards. Image source, Local Democracy Reporting Service Image caption, Visitors are being urged to respect the landscape and take their litter home Karen O'Connor, who has lived near the reservoir for 35 years, said increasing visitor numbers had made conditions worse - and she worried about emergency access. evidence_packet.summary: A drone unit at Greater Manchester Police is regularly following and helping to catch criminals
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police says drones are 'future of policing' - BBC News Image source, Greater Manchester Police Image caption, Police have been using drones to track down bike thieves across the north of Manchester By Richard Stead North West Published 26 August 2026 Drones have been described a "the future of policing" after they were used to help seize 130 illegal off-road bikes across north Manchester in the less than a year. The fleet of drones is being used by Greater Manchester Police instead of the force helicopter because drones are cheaper to use and more discreet. Insp Dan Pickavance, from GMP's North Manchester Neighbourhood Policing Team, said: "All police forces can use drones - particularly in urban areas - and it means we can safely take illegal off-road bikes off the streets. "Using drones is without doubt the future of neighbourhood policing and this is an essential game-changer for us going forward." Image caption, Dan Pickavance, a neighbourhood police inspector for North Manchester, was able to monitor the images from the drone The BBC followed a police operation in which a drone was used to recover a stolen bike that had been spotted in Boggart Hole Clough. The drone was used to follow the bike to an address in nearby Charlestown, where police officers on the ground searched the property and arrested three suspects. The operation was directed by a senior police officer in the back of a van, using live images from the drone which were relayed onto a screen. title: Kimpton Clocktower workers to strike during Manchester Pride

evidence_packet.title: Kimpton Clocktower workers to strike during Manchester Pride
evidence_packet.lead: The action will mark the first ever hospitality strike in the North West, according to the union
evidence_packet.summary: The action will mark the first ever hospitality strike in the North West, according to the union
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Staff at a Manchester hotel will be on strike during the city's upcoming Pride weekend Unite union members working at the Kimpton Clocktower hotel and its bar, The Refuge, will be striking over working conditions on Saturday - the second day of Manchester Pride The strike will mark the first ever hospitality strike in the North West, according to the union. It comes after the hotel advertised Pride weekend package stays and a free two-day Pride celebration to take place at the hotel's Refuge bar A spokesperson for InterContinental Hotels Group UK (IHG), which owns the Kimpton Clocktower, said it has plans to minimise disruption - adding "the hotel and The Refuge continue to operate as normal" "We are aware of concerns raised by a small number of colleagues at The Refuge at the Kimpton Clocktower Manchester, who have decided to take industrial action," the IHG spokesperson said "We have taken those concerns seriously and continue to engage with colleagues through well established, direct feedback channels."

The issue is now being escalated by Stockport council over fears more than £40m could be lost The Stockport 8 development is one of the largest town centre regeneration projects in the UK. It could see over £350m of investment, and include 1,300 homes as well as new businesses It is part of plans by Stockport Council to completely transform the town with thousands of new homes The development covers a large area to the west of the town’s iconic railway viaduct between the now-finished Weir Mill scheme and the central railway station. Phase 1 of the scheme will include a mixed residential neighbourhood of 435 homes and 82 affordable properties It was hoped the first phase of the scheme would start construction in 2026 but the plans could now be delayed. evidence_packet.evidence_text: I've had no front doorway for over 12 months... it's been 26 years of hell' Dad-of-three James Johnstone blames a 26-year-old sewage leak for his problems, but United Utilities don't agree Family say they've been living above a sewer for 26 years Com Speaking to the Manchester Evening News , James Johnstone said he can no longer welcome guests through his front door after his hallway caved in during October last year. The 57-year-old believes the issue is caused by an unused pipe that has been funnelling waste water into his But United Utilities say wastewater from their system has not entered James' home, and is instead 'ground water' linked to historical problems with his property James moved into the Denton home back in 1996. However, he claims issues started to arise by 2000. He told the MEN he uncovered an unused underground pipe behind his home that he believes was the source of the flooding that was blighting his property James says he has approached United Utilities several times over the situation. And the dad-of-three says multiple engineers have carried out work on the system near his home, but nothing so far has addressed the main issue "I've had no front doorway for over a year," he said. Police went to his home in Wakefield, West Yorkshire, just a few hours later and seized his mobile device. The CPS said it then emerged that a second threatening phone call was made Levy, who is Jewish, called the Iqra Mosque in Longsight on the same day and told a member of staff: "I am going to kill you Muslim" In a statement, the CPS said he admitted to being angry after watching news coverage of the October 2 synagogue attack, in which two men were killed at Heaton Park Hebrew Synagogue in Crumpsall. Levy pleaded guilty to making threats to kill and was sentenced on Wednesday at Leeds

evidence_packet.lead: Stockport The £41m row between Stagecoach and Stockport council Stagecoach said they were having 'positive discussions' but Stockport council has accused them of asking for too much money for two depots Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Repo Stagecoach is being accused
evidence_packet.summary: Stockport The £41m row between Stagecoach and Stockport council Stagecoach said they were having 'positive discussions' but Stockport council has accused them of asking for too much money for two depots Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Repo Stagecoach is being accused
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport The £41m row between Stagecoach and Stockport council Stagecoach said they were having 'positive discussions' but Stockport council has accused them of asking for too much money for two depots Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Repo Stagecoach is being accused of holding up major plans to revive Stockport town centre, amid claims the bus company asking for too much money. The issue is now being escalated by Stockport council over fears more than £40m could be lost The Stockport 8 development is one of the largest town centre regeneration projects in the UK. It could see over £350m of investment, and include 1,300 homes as well as new businesses It is part of plans by Stockport Council to completely transform the town with thousands of new homes The development covers a large area to the west of the town’s iconic railway viaduct between the now-finished Weir Mill scheme and the central railway station. Phase 1 of the scheme will include a mixed residential neighbourhood of 435 homes and 82 affordable properties It was hoped the first phase of the scheme would start construction in 2026 but the plans could now be delayed. This is because Stagecoach are asking for too much money in relation to their depots in the town centre, according to a new Stockport council report

evidence_packet.lead: Rochdale 'I thought I was going to drop dead': The NHS worker saved from a hidden 'widow maker' A day out at a soft play centre almost ended in tragedy for Martin Buckley.
evidence_packet.summary: Rochdale 'I thought I was going to drop dead': The NHS worker saved from a hidden 'widow maker' A day out at a soft play centre almost ended in tragedy for Martin Buckley. After going into sudden heart failure, gaining seven stone from fear, and battl Comments News Lee Grimsditch
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rochdale 'I thought I was going to drop dead': The NHS worker saved from a hidden 'widow maker' A day out at a soft play centre almost ended in tragedy for Martin Buckley. After going into sudden heart failure, gaining seven stone from fear, and battl Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 05:52, 27 Aug 2026 Martin Buckley's story is the fourteenth in the Manchester Evening News' Survivors series, featuring interviews with remarkable people who have survived traumatic experiences Many never get the chance to hear terrifying news, doctors told Martin. Back in 2019, aged 35, he and his wife had offered to take a friend's young son for a day out at a soft play centre in Manchester - as they often did Amid the children's laughter and noise, he began to feel as though something wasn't quite right. "He was off playing," Martin said. "I'd gone back to my wife, got drinks or something, and then I went back to find him "And as I've seen him, I've gone towards him, and I've ducked under a bridge that was in there. As soon as I kind of bent down to go underneath it, something just happened in my heart." Martin, who works in IT for the NHS, describes the sensation as his heart 'skipping a beat', adding: "I didn't feel great so I went back to my wife and I'm like, I don't feel good, I don't feel right."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: I've had no front doorway for over 12 months... it's been 26 years of hell' Dad-of-three James Johnstone blames a 26-year-old sewage leak for his problems, but United Utilities don't agree Family say they've been living above a sewer for 26 years Com Speaking to the Manchester Evening News , James Johnstone said he can no longer welcome guests through his front door after his hallway caved in during October last year. The 57-year-old believes the issue is caused by an unused pipe that has been funnelling waste water into his But United Utilities say wastewater from their system has not entered James' home, and is instead 'ground water' linked to historical problems with his property James moved into the Denton home back in 1996. However, he claims issues started to arise by 2000. He told the MEN he uncovered an unused underground pipe behind his home that he believes was the source of the flooding that was blighting his property James says he has approached United Utilities several times over the situation. And the dad-of-three says multiple engineers have carried out work on the system near his home, but nothing so far has addressed the main issue "I've had no front doorway for over a year," he said. " My floor and my hallway fell into what used to be the cellar."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police GMP's facial recognition leads to first arrest from new alert system The LFR van was stationed at Manchester Victoria News Elizabeth Cotton TV and Celebrity Writer 17:55, 26 Aug 2026 View 2 Images A GMP van was deployed to Ma GMP’s latest Live Facial Recognition (LFR) operation led to several arrests on Wednesday, August 25, including the force’s first arrest following an alert linked to a Serious Crime Prevention Order The LFR van was stationed at Manchester Victoria throughout parts of the morning and afternoon, scanning the area for individuals on pre-set watchlists. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts 'Angry' man made terrifying threats to Manchester mosque two days after synagogue terror attack 'I'm going to come to your mosque and kill you' News Paul Britton Reporter 13:31, 26 Aug 2026 View 2 Images Gabriel Levy (Image: CPS) A man who made death threats to two mosques in Manchester days after the Heaton Park synagogue terror attack has been jailed Gabriel Levy, 21, made an anonymous phone call to the Al-Sunnah Mosque in Cheetham Hill on the afternoon of October 4, 2025, the Crown Prosecution Service said. Using a withheld number, he told the call receiver: "I'm going to come to your mosque and kill you." Police went to his home in Wakefield, West Yorkshire, just a few hours later and seized his mobile device. The CPS said it then emerged that a second threatening phone call was made Levy, who is Jewish, called the Iqra Mosque in Longsight on the same day and told a member of staff: "I am going to kill you Muslim" In a statement, the CPS said he admitted to being angry after watching news coverage of the October 2 synagogue attack, in which two men were killed at Heaton Park Hebrew Synagogue in Crumpsall. Levy pleaded guilty to making threats to kill and was sentenced on Wednesday at Leeds

Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 07: A row over the future of Market Street has taken another twist after a second petition was launched, making demands of the council The new petition has just nine signatures so far and is calling to ‘protect and support Market Street stalls’ and ‘keep fresh sweetcorn in the city centre’ It comes after another petition was launched last month calling for a review of Market Street and Piccadilly Gardens . The petition, which more than 600 people have put their names to, calls for a major revamp of the space to make it more organised and easier to use and tackle th Now, a new petition seeking to support traders has been set up by Muhammad Adnan. They provide affordable, fresh sweetcorn and street food for families, workers, and tourists "Removing them takes away vibrancy, jobs, and choice. We the people of Manchester ask Manchester City Council to protect and support Market Street stalls."

evidence_packet.lead: I've had no front doorway for over 12 months...
evidence_packet.summary: I've had no front doorway for over 12 months... it's been 26 years of hell' Dad-of-three James Johnstone blames a 26-year-old sewage leak for his problems, but United Utilities don't agree Family say they've been living above a sewer for 26 years Com Speaking to the Manchester Ev
evidence_packet.evidence_text: I've had no front doorway for over 12 months... it's been 26 years of hell' Dad-of-three James Johnstone blames a 26-year-old sewage leak for his problems, but United Utilities don't agree Family say they've been living above a sewer for 26 years Com Speaking to the Manchester Evening News , James Johnstone said he can no longer welcome guests through his front door after his hallway caved in during October last year. The 57-year-old believes the issue is caused by an unused pipe that has been funnelling waste water into his But United Utilities say wastewater from their system has not entered James' home, and is instead 'ground water' linked to historical problems with his property James moved into the Denton home back in 1996. However, he claims issues started to arise by 2000. He told the MEN he uncovered an unused underground pipe behind his home that he believes was the source of the flooding that was blighting his property James says he has approached United Utilities several times over the situation. And the dad-of-three says multiple engineers have carried out work on the system near his home, but nothing so far has addressed the main issue "I've had no front doorway for over a year," he said. " My floor and my hallway fell into what used to be the cellar."

The issue is now being escalated by Stockport council over fears more than £40m could be lost The Stockport 8 development is one of the largest town centre regeneration projects in the UK. It could see over £350m of investment, and include 1,300 homes as well as new businesses It is part of plans by Stockport Council to completely transform the town with thousands of new homes The development covers a large area to the west of the town’s iconic railway viaduct between the now-finished Weir Mill scheme and the central railway station. Phase 1 of the scheme will include a mixed residential neighbourhood of 435 homes and 82 affordable properties It was hoped the first phase of the scheme would start construction in 2026 but the plans could now be delayed. title: 'I thought I was going to drop dead': The NHS worker saved from a hidden 'widow maker'

evidence_packet.title: 'I thought I was going to drop dead': The NHS worker saved from a hidden 'widow maker'
evidence_packet.lead: Rochdale 'I thought I was going to drop dead': The NHS worker saved from a hidden 'widow maker' A day out at a soft play centre almost ended in tragedy for Martin Buckley.
evidence_packet.summary: Rochdale 'I thought I was going to drop dead': The NHS worker saved from a hidden 'widow maker' A day out at a soft play centre almost ended in tragedy for Martin Buckley. After going into sudden heart failure, gaining seven stone from fear, and battl Comments News Lee Grimsditch
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rochdale 'I thought I was going to drop dead': The NHS worker saved from a hidden 'widow maker' A day out at a soft play centre almost ended in tragedy for Martin Buckley. After going into sudden heart failure, gaining seven stone from fear, and battl Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 05:52, 27 Aug 2026 Martin Buckley's story is the fourteenth in the Manchester Evening News' Survivors series, featuring interviews with remarkable people who have survived traumatic experiences Many never get the chance to hear terrifying news, doctors told Martin. Back in 2019, aged 35, he and his wife had offered to take a friend's young son for a day out at a soft play centre in Manchester - as they often did Amid the children's laughter and noise, he began to feel as though something wasn't quite right. "He was off playing," Martin said. "I'd gone back to my wife, got drinks or something, and then I went back to find him "And as I've seen him, I've gone towards him, and I've ducked under a bridge that was in there. As soon as I kind of bent down to go underneath it, something just happened in my heart." Martin, who works in IT for the NHS, describes the sensation as his heart 'skipping a beat', adding: "I didn't feel great so I went back to my wife and I'm like, I don't feel good, I don't feel right."

title: Why NHS staff at four Greater Manchester hospitals have gone on strike

evidence_packet.title: Why NHS staff at four Greater Manchester hospitals have gone on strike
evidence_packet.lead: NHS Why NHS staff at four Greater Manchester hospitals have gone on strike Hospital staff say they are being pushed to work overtime for less money as staffing shortages, burnout and patient safety fears fuel an ongoing dispute with a Greater Manchest Outside Salford Royal, cars
evidence_packet.summary: NHS Why NHS staff at four Greater Manchester hospitals have gone on strike Hospital staff say they are being pushed to work overtime for less money as staffing shortages, burnout and patient safety fears fuel an ongoing dispute with a Greater Manchest Outside Salford Royal, cars
evidence_packet.evidence_text: NHS Why NHS staff at four Greater Manchester hospitals have gone on strike Hospital staff say they are being pushed to work overtime for less money as staffing shortages, burnout and patient safety fears fuel an ongoing dispute with a Greater Manchest Outside Salford Royal, cars honked in support of hundreds of NHS workers as they stood on the picket line in purple ponchos - and the rain poured Theatre staff at four NHS hospitals across Greater Manchester have walked out for a second day this week in an ongoing dispute about overtime pay More than 350 employees at Northern Care Alliance Foundation Trust (NCA) - including nurses, clinical support workers and housekeepers - staged strike action on Monday (August 24) and Wednesday (August 26), and will walk out again on Friday (August 28) Those striking work across Salford Royal Hospital, Royal Oldham Hospital, Rochdale Infirmary and Fairfield Hospital in Bury It comes as the NCA has been criticised over patient safety concerns , with public records by the Trust showing dozens of patients have died or come to harm due to treatment delays and serious errors made by staff working under extreme pressure

Police later discovered a converted gun in a flat in Radcliffe where Hanson stored cocaine and cannabis for onward sale Previously, the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said it has launched an investigation into the firearms operation which ended in Hanson being shot During a sentencing hearing today, (August 26) Manchester Crown Court heard that Hanson, now 20, has been dealing cannabis since the age of 14, and had been trying to sell the gun prior to its seizure He will learn his fate tomorrow (August 27) after pleading guilty to drug and firearms charges. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police GMP's facial recognition leads to first arrest from new alert system The LFR van was stationed at Manchester Victoria News Elizabeth Cotton TV and Celebrity Writer 17:55, 26 Aug 2026 View 2 Images A GMP van was deployed to Ma GMP’s latest Live Facial Recognition (LFR) operation led to several arrests on Wednesday, August 25, including the force’s first arrest following an alert linked to a Serious Crime Prevention Order The LFR van was stationed at Manchester Victoria throughout parts of the morning and afternoon, scanning the area for individuals on pre-set watchlists. These can include people wanted in connection with offences, registered sex offenders, missing people and others of interest Among those identified was a 46-year-old man who was arrested on suspicion of breaching a Serious Crime Prevention Order (SCPO), marking the first time an LFR alert has resulted in an arrest for an alleged SCPO breach Officers found the man carrying a number of mobile phones, tablets, passports and bank cards, which were believed to be in breach of conditions imposed on him by the courts. evidence_packet.summary: Courts 'Angry' man made terrifying threats to Manchester mosque two days after synagogue terror attack 'I'm going to come to your mosque and kill you' News Paul Britton Reporter 13:31, 26 Aug 2026 View 2 Images Gabriel Levy (Image: CPS) A man who made death threats to two mosques
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts 'Angry' man made terrifying threats to Manchester mosque two days after synagogue terror attack 'I'm going to come to your mosque and kill you' News Paul Britton Reporter 13:31, 26 Aug 2026 View 2 Images Gabriel Levy (Image: CPS) A man who made death threats to two mosques in Manchester days after the Heaton Park synagogue terror attack has been jailed Gabriel Levy, 21, made an anonymous phone call to the Al-Sunnah Mosque in Cheetham Hill on the afternoon of October 4, 2025, the Crown Prosecution Service said. Using a withheld number, he told the call receiver: "I'm going to come to your mosque and kill you." Police went to his home in Wakefield, West Yorkshire, just a few hours later and seized his mobile device. The CPS said it then emerged that a second threatening phone call was made Levy, who is Jewish, called the Iqra Mosque in Longsight on the same day and told a member of staff: "I am going to kill you Muslim" In a statement, the CPS said he admitted to being angry after watching news coverage of the October 2 synagogue attack, in which two men were killed at Heaton Park Hebrew Synagogue in Crumpsall. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Radcliffe Radcliffe man, 22, ends up in court after chat with cyclist left them 'backing away in fear' Tyreece Bedford appeared at Manchester Crown Court Comments News Hope Gallagher 06:00, 26 Aug 2026 View 2 Images Tyreece Bedford A man swiped a man's hat after pulling out what police believe was a knife. Tyreece Bedford, 22, found himself in the dock following the 'tomfoolery' last summer Manchester Crown Court heard a man he knew cycled past him on Pilkington Way, Radcliffe , on June 14, 2025. The cyclist turned back and approached Bedford The pair briefly spoke before Bedford took the man's hat. When he tried to get it back, Bedford brandished an object cops believe was a blade CCTV footage played in court showed the man backing away from Bedford. He was initially charged with threatening a person with a blade and theft, but instead pleaded guilty to the lesser charge of affray Prosecutor Brian Berlyne said: "The man backed away in apparent fear. He appears to believe it to be a weapon. Police believe it to have been a small knife."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Friday 31 July 2026 at 11:11pm More than two million voters were eligible to vote in the Greater Manchester mayoral by-election as counting getsunderway. Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

Within days she was placed in an induced coma and transferred to the specialist liver intensive care unit at Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham, one of only a handful of c On 22 July a donor liver became available, but during the operation she suffered three cardiac arrests after a blood clot blocked the main artery to her lungs, leaving her starved of oxygen for a prolonged period. Surgeons told her husband Ollie more than once that she was unlike Against the odds she pulled through. Six weeks on she is conscious and recognises her family, but the lack of oxygen caused significant brain damage to both sides of her brain. She cannot move, remains on a ventilator and dialysis, and is still in critical care “She’s conscious. She is recognising who we are,” Ollie said. “She’s saying the odd word, albeit very, very weak. evidence_packet.evidence_text: on WhatsApp Share via Email A blue plaque has been unveiled at a Bowdon house to mark the life of William Wood, the social reformer known as “The Climbing Boys’ Friend” The plaque is at Willow Cottage, 28 Stamford Road, where Wood lived after retiring there in 1847. It was unveiled last week at a ceremony organised by Trafford Council’s Local Studies team, attended by residents, historians, council members, Connor Rand MP and the Friends of Bowd Wood, born in 1782, was a wool merchant who began campaigning in 1826 after seeing a young boy fall to his death inside a chimney onto a live fire. “Climbing boys” were children sent up chimneys to sweep them, often suffering burns, respiratory illness, deformity and suffocation From Bowdon he funded prosecutions against master sweeps who broke child labour laws, put up placards at railway stations and wrote to newspapers He also challenged magistrates and even Queen Victoria over the use of a child sweep at Windsor Castle His work with Lord Shaftesbury included testimony to the House of Lords in 1853, which helped lead to the Chimney Sweepers Act of 1875. Wood died in 1868, aged 85, seven years before the practice was banned. Six chimney sweeps from five towns carried his coffin to St Mary’s Churc

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Pho Cue heads for the edge of the Peak District with a modern Vietnamese menu made for the grills Go to Manchester's Finest X profile You don’t have to work too hard to sell Pho Cue to anyone who eats out in Manchester regularly. Hidden in plain sight in Chinatown, it’s the kind of place chefs recommend, food writers praise, and regulars quietly keep going back to Jay Rayner called it “everything it should be” when he visited in 2021, which is about right. It’s intimate, informal, very good value and usually busy enough to make you feel smug if you’ve managed to get a table without waiting The pho is obviously a very good choice. So are the bánh mì. So is most of the menu, to be honest. But for the next Open Fire Dining Club , Pho Cue are stepping out of Chinatown and heading to Torr Vale Mill for something a little different They’ll be joining Tartuffe on 22 and 23 August for a menu that looks at Vietnamese cooking through a few different routes: the French influence that still runs through parts of the cuisine, the traditional use of fire found across Vietnam, and Cue’s more modern approach to Vietn There’s a continuation from the Porta dinner here too. That menu touched on the French influence in Basque cooking; this one takes the same idea in a different direction, from bánh mì and pâté to grilled meats, broths, herbs, sharp dressings and coffee. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Hilton House keeps proving itself as one of the borough's best creative hubs and this August it's hosting a community music night. PINK's Summer Open Mic is being put on by local guitar shop Rigby Music, with covers and originals welcome from anyone who wants to give it a go Alongside the music, fellow Hilton House residents Spearpoint Vintage are setting up a pop-up of pieces from their collection, available to buy on the night, with the chance to book in for a future appointment at their showroom too It's a relaxed one — no pressure, just a room of people who like music and a rail of good vintage to pick through between sets Where: PINK, Hilton House, Lord Street, Stockport SK1 3NA When: Wednesday 5 August 2026, 6:45pm–10pm Want to perform? Email admin@rigbymusic.co.uk Know of an open mic or pop-up we should be covering? Let us know — we're always up for a Wednesday night out in the borough

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Totally Stockport has launched a new masterplan as part of its Going Green programme, setting out a bold and practical vision for a greener, healthier and more vibrant town centre Developed by Layer.studio in consultation with retailers and residents, ‘Going Green’ focuses on the places people use every day and sets out a strategy, toolkit and initial projects to support regeneration, wellbeing and economic activity With the aim to create a connected, people-focused green infrastructure network, streets, squares and key routes have been reviewed to create a one connected green network The masterplan spans the 80Ha Totally Stockport BID Boundary and combines quick wins with longer-term visions in key areas, setting out a practical route to a town centre that’s even more walkable, attractive and economically active Paul Kelsall, BID Director at Totally Stockport and co-owner of Stockport based Kelsall Architects, said: “At its core, ‘Going Green’ is about joining the green dots “From Merseyway to the Underbanks and Chestergate, the masterplan shows how simple, well-placed changes such as more planting and enhanced greenery can change the face of the town centre

For over ten years Manchester Digital That gap has become harder to bridge, economic uncertainty, higher costs and cautious hiring are playing their part as is AI, which is starting to strip out the routine tasks junior roles were built on. This has resulted in the entry-level jobs young people used to start in being Alan Milburn's interim review, published in May, put a shortage of entry-level jobs at the centre of a "generational fault line", with one in eight young people now not in education, employment or training. This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Flower Festival returns 23–25 May 2026 with floral displays, events and a city-wide trail Manchester Flower Festival returns 23–25 May 2026 with floral displays, events and a city-wide trail For one weekend in May, the city centre won’t just be somewhere to shop, eat and pass through. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bouaddi joined the Blues today from Lille on a five-year-contact as the fourth signing of the summer after the arrivals of Elliot Anderson, Jeremy Monga and Gerónimo Rulli. The 18-year-old joins as one of the most exciting young players in world football having made 96 appearances for Lille and won eight international caps already for Morocco including a starring role in this summer’s World Cup. evidence_packet.evidence_text: 8 ноября 2026 года в Indigo at The O2 состоится концерт GORAN BREGOVIC в Лондоне Имя Горана Бреговича давно стало символом целого музыкального мира. Его путь начался в многонациональном Сараеве, где восточные мотивы естественно переплетались с западными традициями, а каждая улица имела свой ритм. Именно эта атмосфера сформировала композитора, впоследствии воз Впоследствии музыка Бреговича вышла за рамки концертных площадок. Сотрудничество с режиссером Emir Kusturica подарило мировому кинематографу саундтреки, ставшие неотъемлемой частью фильмов Time of the Gypsies, Arizona Dream и Underground. В этих мелодиях живут Балканы — с их своб Популярность Бреговича родилась не только благодаря знаменитым композициям “Kalashnikov”, “Ederlezi”, “In the Death Car” или “Bella Ciao”. Его главный талант — превращать народные мотивы в современное искусство, не теряя их подлинной силы. Город, который веками принимал выступления и разные культуры со всех континентов, на один вечер станет местом встречи британской сдержанности и безудержной балканской страсти. evidence_packet.summary: Приготовьтесь к незабываемому вечеру с одной из самых любимых звезд турецкой поп-сцены — Муратом Далкылычем, в Лондоне! После выхода хита «Kasaba» в 2008 году Мурат Далкылыч стал одной из главных фигур турецкой поп-музыки
evidence_packet.evidence_text: --> Murat Dalkılıç в Лондон ᐉ Билет на концерт Купить на 29 января 2027 ᐉ mticket.uk --> --> КОНЦЕРТЫ ТУРЫ ТЕАТР Добавить событие Условия использования Политика конфиденциальности Помощь --> --> --> --> --> --> --> --> --> --> --> --> Личный кабинет Контакты --> --> 189279-136115 Афиша Великобритания » Лондон » КОНЦЕРТЫ » Indigo at The O2 » Murat Dalkılıç 47,70-90,10 GBP Купить билет #Поп #Поп-рок #Dance-Pop 29 января Murat Dalkılıç Лондон 47,70-90,10 GBP Лондон Indigo at The O2 205 Peninsula Square, London SE10 0ES, Great Britain Купить билет Поделиться в соцсетях Заказать билеты на "Murat Dalkılıç" Выбрать дату 29 янв. пятница --> --> --> 20:30 Открытие дверей: 19:00 47,70-90,10 GBP Купить билет О событии Приготовьтесь к незабываемому вечеру с одной из самых любимых звезд турецкой поп-сцены — Муратом Далкылычем, в Лондоне! После выхода хита «Kasaba» в 2008 году Мурат Далкылыч стал одной из главных фигур турецкой поп-музыки. Он известен своим узнаваемым голосом, энергичными выступлениями и популярными песнями, среди которых «Bir Güzellik Yap». За годы карьеры в музыке, написании песен и кино он приобрел большую и преданную аудиторию как в Турции, так и за ее пределами. 29 января 2027 года Мурат Далкылыч выступит в indigo at The O2 в Лондоне. Вас ждет яркий вечер турецкой поп-музыки, живого исполнения и любимых хитов. Не упустите возможность увидеть Мурата Далкылыча вживую в Лондоне! Предварительный заказ

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Events EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters Official Chamber Post FREE Online Thursday 10 Sep 10am - 11am Book Now About the event The way low-value goods enter the European Union is changing From 1 July 2026, the EU introduced a new €3 customs duty on low-value consignments valued up to €150 entering the EU from outside the bloc. The change removes the previous duty exemption and introduces new considerations for businesses exporting goods directly to EU customers The new duty applies based on product categories/tariff classifications rather than simply per parcel, meaning shipments containing different types of goods could face multiple charges. For example, a parcel containing products under different tariff headings may attract multiple While the change is aimed largely at addressing the growth of low-value e-commerce imports, it will also impact UK businesses selling products directly into EU markets, including online retailers, brands and SMEs What the new €3 EU customs duty means for UK businesses
